source_acquisition.search_note: The automated visual_source_inventory row says no_public_source_found and the local corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-eb5aba1da40d directory is absent. arXiv 2603.08859 was confirmed; unicli scholar code did not return a resource and OpenReview lookup had expired authentication. GitHub search and tree inspection identified the author repository SprocketLab/hybrid-expressivity (main revision 7beeb0de80f89eb9b36ca999, README says it contains the associated paper experiments). Its micro_hf, micro, mini, and constructions sources cover result assets and construction heatmaps; Figure 5, 6, 15, and 16 assets were RGB-pixel matched to the PDF extractions. Figure 1–3 original diagram sources and the paper TeX were not found. The MachineLearning-Nerd repository is an independent reproduction audit, not used for visual attribution.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Result plots use a fixed categorical architecture palette (blue/orange/red/green); Figure 8 uses blue/green/red for T_rope/hybrid/mamba; construction heatmaps use a discrete viridis-like purple/cyan/yellow value key. Color is usually not redundantly encoded by shape or marker.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figures 2–3 are predominantly PDF vector paths/text; Figure 1, all Matplotlib result charts, and Figures 9–10 are embedded raster images, while captions, table rules, and page text remain PDF objects. pdfimages reports chart rasters at roughly 185–462 ppi and Figure 1 at 394 ppi.
paper_style.style_consistency: Single-column article layout is consistent across 29 physical pages. Computer Modern dominates page text/math; DejaVu Sans dominates raster plots. The shared result palette, dashed grids, and same-color bands are coherent, but duplicated legends, color-only coding, and uneven caption statistics reduce accessibility and self-containment.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Example function composition task. The answer to a learned question only depends on a part of the long context input.

figures.data_and_statistics: No experimental sample or aggregation. A qualitative basketball-question example makes long-context input, relevant fragment, function composition, and answer nodes concrete.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction function-composition claim → Figure 1 visualizes long-context extraction and local answer dependence → Figure 2 abstracts the SSM-to-Transformer interface → Figures 4–8 and Table 1 test learned models.
design_strengths: Concrete basketball example lowers the entry cost of the abstract function-composition setup.
Arrows, answer bubbles, and central model support a clear left-to-right/downward reading.
design_weaknesses: Small raster text and color-heavy semantic distinctions reduce accessibility in a single-column reproduction.
Caption omits the color key and does not explicitly map the two branches to the later u/v notation.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a concrete semantic example to show long-context extraction → local addressing → function composition → answer; add a caption key and formal-symbol mapping for reuse.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: The construction’s style follows taking an input x and implementing 2 functions u, v with an SSM. Typically, u is a truncation of the input, and v is a control parameter (represented in purple). Lastly, a Transformer combines these by implementing F to perform the complete task (represented in red).

encodings.text: x, u, v, SSM, TF, and F labels

figures.data_and_statistics: No observations or summary statistics. This is an interface diagram for x → (u,v) → F and the division of labor between SSM extraction and Transformer composition.
figures.evidence_relation: Theorems 3.3/3.7 preview pure-model resource bottlenecks → Section 4 defines SSM_u/SSM_v and TF readout → Figure 2 makes that interface inspectable → Figure 3 instantiates Selective Copy.

The control/output color key directly bridges the schematic to the accompanying formulas.
design_weaknesses: No state size, context window, layer count, or parameter-cost annotation is shown.
Color remains the primary distinction for truncation/control/output and is weak under grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Split an encoder and local composition stage into explicit upstream/downstream boxes, marking a control token and final output while listing the resource boundary nearby.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 grounds long-context function composition in a basketball example; Figures 2–3 formalize the SSM-first interface and Selective Copy mechanism; Figures 4–8 and Table 1 carry the interface into learned comparisons and generalization; Figures 9–10 show construction matrices; Figures 11–16 test vocabulary, capacity, adversarial distribution, and window boundaries.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All 18 objects use a conventional caption beginning with Figure/Table label. Mechanism and heatmap captions explain setup and encodings better than most result captions. Results commonly state a finding but omit color keys, band/run definitions, denominators, or fixed conditions; Figures 12 and 16 are exceptions that define 0.1/0.9 quantiles.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 uses one header row (Train Proportion / SSM / TF / Hybrid) and puts the fixed evaluation condition in its caption; Table 2 uses Symbol / Meaning as a glossary header. Figure 4 and 6 embed analogous architecture columns inside charts, but those embedded tables are part of the figures rather than separate PDF tables.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figures 2–3 connect theorem-level u/v extraction and relative lookup to the learned frontiers in Figures 4–8; Figures 11–16 then vary vocabulary, heads, state, mixture distribution, and window to distinguish resource limits from learnability effects.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figures 4–8 and Table 1 carry the principal learned evidence; Appendix Figures 9–10 expose the construction implementation and Figures 11–16 stress-test the same claims under additional capacity, distribution, and context settings. Appendix E.1 supplies statistical conventions needed to interpret most bands.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Page-level text, captions, equations, and tables use Computer Modern-derived fonts, while raster plot labels use DejaVu Sans. Approximate plot text sizing and scaling are stable across result assets, with smaller final labels than the notebook rcParams suggest.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/orange/red/green consistently identify architecture sequences across the micro_hf results, and blue/green/red identify T_rope/hybrid/mamba in Figure 8. Heatmaps intentionally switch to a discrete value palette with an explicit caption key. Neither family has robust shape/line redundancy.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 2’s explicit SSM encoder → Transformer composer interface maps theory symbols to implementation roles.
Figures 4 and 6 combine parameter-frontier curves with compact exact-value tables.
Figures 9 and 10 use matched input/output heatmaps and one discrete color grammar for construction reproduction.
Figures 11, 12, and 16 use side-by-side panels to separate vocabulary or capacity axes.
Figure 13’s caption names both adversarial failure modes instead of hiding the stress-test setup.
highest_value_objects: Figure 4 for the direct Selective Copy efficiency headline.
Figure 6 for the MKAR frontier and six-fold parameter anchor.
failure_patterns: Architecture identity is mostly color-only, reducing grayscale and color-vision accessibility.
Most result captions omit band definition, run count, denominator, or fixed comparison conditions.
Figures 11, 12, and 16 repeat legends and sacrifice plot area.
Table 1 provides no uncertainty, while Figures 14–15 omit their most informative window-degradation conclusion.
Figure 1–3 original visual sources are unavailable, and the current micro source has a version-specific aggregation naming mismatch for Figure 13.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use a concrete concept diagram and SSM→TF architecture to establish function-composition roles, parameter-frontier plots and anchor tables for the main comparisons, then matched construction heatmaps and capacity/distribution/window ablations to expose reproducibility and learnability boundaries; improve the system by defining colors, bands, references, and comparison conditions at object level.
